newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-Northland the underdogs for 2nd div final.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Northland the underdogs for 2nd div final.

text.p: WHANGAREI, Oct 25 - Northland, making their second successive appearance in the NPC second division rugby final, face the double task of beating both their playoff jinx as well as Southland in tomorrow's final at Homestead Stadium, Invercargill, NZPA reports.
The form book, the TAB betting desk, most rugby pundits throughout the country and thousands of Southlanders all say they can't do it.

The Northland team are under no illusions as to the enormity of the challenge and acknowledge that as a result of their 34-14 loss to Southland two weeks ago and that they are again playing in Invercargill, they are very much the underdogs.
Northland have opted for a low key approach.
The side had their final training run in Christchurch late yesterday afternoon, on a ground at Burnside Park which didn't have any ground markings or goalposts.
"But it was all we needed," coach Sid Going said.
"The run went pretty well, obviously everyone is getting keyed up, we're all feeling the pressure. The game means so much."
Second five-eighths Brandon Reid and blindside flanker Justin Collins, who both missed last Sunday's semifinal against Manawatu because of injury, are back in the starting line-up for the final.
They were initially bracketed with the players who took their places on Sunday -- Duncan Bell and Richard Hilton-Jones -- but last night Going confirmed Reid and Collins would start.
Bell and Hilton-Jones are in the reserves.
Lineout leapers Glenn Taylor and Norman Maxwell probably hold the key for Northland.
They are well capable of gaining a distinct edge despite being opposed by two equally big men in Mark Tinnock and Andrew Campbell.

If Northland learnt anything from their loss in Invercargill two weeks go and from the hard-fought semifinal last Sunday it must be that they can't afford to shy off tackles and they must cut basic errors to a minimum.
"We've got just 80 minutes to go, we haven't played to our potential yet and if we do then we can win," Going said.
He added that Northland didn't play at all well two weeks ago.
"With improved application and attitude we'll do much better.
"What we need is a total performance not just one when we go well in patches.
"We have strengths right through the team and we haven't always played to them," he said.
For four years the Northland team, under Going, has been striving to get back into the top echelon of New Zealand rugby.
